Geoinformatics × credit risk

When the climate shifts, credit risk shifts with it.

ClimaRisk Tunisia links every loan in a portfolio to its exposure to heat, drought, floods and wildfire, today, in 2030 and in 2050.

ClimaRisk Tunisia · 100 % synthetic portfolio1 / 7
The method

From satellite pixels to expected loss, in four steps

1
Portfolio

2,000 synthetic loans placed across 24 governorates using population (WorldPop) and cropland (ESA WorldCover).

2
Hazard

Days above 35 °C and drought (5 CMIP6 models, NASA), 100-year flood depth (WRI Aqueduct), burnable vegetation.

3
Vulnerability

Each sector weights the hazards: rain-fed cereals fear drought, coastal hotels fear flooding.

4
Credit

PD′ = PD × (1 + β·score), LGD adjusted for flood depth, EL = PD′ × LGD′ × EAD, aggregated by sector and governorate.

What I learned

An honest tool beats a precise-looking number

  • The PD elasticity (β) matters far more than climate-model uncertainty: it is the first thing to calibrate on observed defaults.
  • Two drought indicators can point to opposite regions: the right one depends on what is being financed.
  • The NGFS Phase V GDP-damage function relies on a retracted paper, so I left it out.
  • Physical risk only, a 25 km climate grid, and a synthetic portfolio.

Website, working paper, code and video: link in the comments.
